# Rewrite history, one order at a time

> Play an experimental AI grand-strategy game with natural-language orders, persistent campaign memory, and 20+ scenarios.

Canonical: https://historia.aliveville.com/

Playable AI grand-strategy experiment

# Open *Historia*

Rewrite history. Command nations in plain English.

Type “invade Bohemia” or “send envoy to the Ottoman court.” An AI Game Master moves armies, shifts treaties, and remembers your campaign across 20+ scenarios from 793 AD to 2040. The core loop is playable; the map and campaign pacing are still prototype-grade.

[Pick a scenario and start](https://historia.aliveville.com/play)

No account required · free AI option · bring your own key · [GitHub repository](https://github.com/sarthakagrawal927/open-historia)

·  THE PITCH  ·

## The world’s most opinionated *Game Master.*

Every Paradox game ships with hard-coded events and scripted ledgers. Open Historia ships with an **LLM**. You type “invade Bohemia” or “send envoy to Ottoman court” and the AI returns the consequences — armies move, treaties shift, relations decay or warm. The Game Master keeps a running summary of your campaign so the world remembers, turn after turn.

The memory works. *The campaign still needs better game feel.*

·  FEATURES  ·

## The working loop. *Still an experiment.*

I

### Multi-provider AI

Use the keyless free option on the web, bring an Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, or DeepSeek key, or connect a local provider when self-hosting.

II

### Save & resume

Play without an account using local saves. Sign in only if you want private cloud saves that follow you across devices.

III

### Alternate history

Rewind to an earlier turn and create a new branch. The Game Master rolls the world forward from your changed decision.

·  LAUNCH  ·

## Try the current build. *Rewrite the rest.*

Choose from 20+ historical, modern, alternate, and fictional presets—or write your own start year, nation, and brief. Expect a working prototype, not a finished grand-strategy game.

[Open the playable prototype](https://historia.aliveville.com/play)

Held project · playable core loop ·

# Steer history, one order at a time

> Learn how Open Historia combines natural-language strategy, an AI rules engine, and rewindable timelines.

Canonical: https://historia.aliveville.com/about

[Open Historia](https://historia.aliveville.com/)

# Steer history, one order at a time.

Open Historia is an open-source AI grand-strategy game. You command a civilization in plain English, and a large-language-model Game Master adjudicates every turn on a living world map.

[Play now — free](https://historia.aliveville.com/play)[How it works](https://historia.aliveville.com/about#how)

No account required. Bring your own AI key, or run a local model.

### Natural-language command

No menus, no build queues. Type what you want — raise an army, broker a marriage alliance, fund a rebellion — and the Game Master works out what happens.

### An AI as the rules engine

There is no hard combat math. A large language model adjudicates every turn, returning a strict-shape JSON contract that updates the map, diplomacy, and the timeline.

### Rewind and branch history

Every turn is a snapshot on the timeline. Rewind to any prior point and branch a new alternate history from there — your choices are never final.

## How a game works

- 01 ### Pick a scenario Start from a historical, modern, alternate, or fictional preset — or write your own. Choose the nation you command and an AI provider.

- 02 ### Issue your orders Queue commands in plain English and advance time. The Game Master returns the consequences: territory changes, events, and shifting relations.

- 03 ### Watch history unfold The world map and diplomacy threads update live. Rewind any turn, branch a new timeline, and save your game to the cloud when signed in.

## Pluggable AI

Pick a provider on game setup — Anthropic Claude, OpenAI, Google Gemini, DeepSeek, or a local OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Your API key stays in your session and is sent only to the provider you chose.

## Saves & alternate timelines

Cloud save when signed in; rewind to any prior turn and branch a new timeline from there. Saves serialize only province ownership, so the format survives changes to the underlying map data.

## What it isn't

- A live multiplayer game. (Yet.)

- A simulation with hard combat math — the LLM is the rules engine, with strict-shape JSON as the contract.

- A chat-with-NPC product. The AI is the world referee, not a character.

## Ready to rewrite history?

Open the map, pick a nation, and give your first order.

[Start a game](https://historia.aliveville.com/play)

# Privacy

> How Open Historia handles sign-in identity, private saves, provider requests, and deletion.

Canonical: https://historia.aliveville.com/privacy

[← Open Historia](https://historia.aliveville.com/)

# Privacy

Last updated: 2026-09-29.

## What we store

- Google OAuth identity (id, name, email, avatar) when you sign in.

- Cloud saves you create — game state, command history, story-so-far.

- An encrypted copy of any API key you save in settings.

- Anonymous website analytics through App Health: page paths, referring hostname, coarse browser/device/country categories, and a project-scoped visitor identifier held in first-party local storage for up to 90 days. The tracker does not store raw IP addresses or user-agent strings and does not set analytics cookies.

- When server endpoint monitoring is enabled, API requests send their method, normalized route template, response status, duration, and declared response byte count to App Health. Request bodies, headers, query values, concrete route parameters, and identity are not included.

## What we don't

- No remarketing tags.

- No sharing of your saves or commands with anyone.

- Guests can play without signing in; nothing is stored server-side.

## LLM provider

When you take a turn the entire game state (you can inspect the JSON payload in your browser's network tab) is sent to whichever provider you've picked on setup. Their privacy policy applies.

## Deletion

Delete individual saves from the timeline panel, or revoke the Google OAuth grant in your account settings to disconnect.

# A free, open-source Pax Historia alternative

> Open Historia is a free, open-source, browser-playable alternative to Pax Historia: natural-language orders, 20+ scenarios, campaign memory, and no credit meter.

Canonical: https://historia.aliveville.com/pax-historia-alternative

[Open Historia](https://historia.aliveville.com/)

# A free, open-source Pax Historia alternative

If you like the idea of an AI-adjudicated alternate-history sandbox but want one you can open in a browser, inspect, and run on your own AI provider — that's what Open Historia is.

[Play in the browser — free](https://historia.aliveville.com/play)[Compare](https://historia.aliveville.com/pax-historia-alternative#compare)

### Plain-English grand strategy

Raise an army, broker an alliance, fund a rebellion — type the order and the Game Master works out what happens on the map.

### 20+ scenarios

Historical, modern, alternate-history, and fictional presets — pick a nation and start a campaign in seconds.

### Rewindable timeline

Every turn is a snapshot. Rewind to any decision and branch a new alternate history from there.

## Open Historia vs. Pax Historia

Pax Historia is a polished hosted platform with a large community. Open Historia is a smaller open-source experiment — the honest trade-offs:

Cost model

Free to play — bring your own AI provider key, a local model, or the shared free gateway. No credit meter.

Hosted platform where play runs through its own service.

Source

MIT-licensed and public on GitHub.

Closed-source platform.

Where it runs

In the browser — nothing to install. Guests play with local saves; optional sign-in adds cloud saves.

Hosted web and mobile apps.

How you play

Type orders in plain English; an AI Game Master adjudicates each turn into map, diplomacy, and timeline changes.

Create, share, and play community-built AI sandbox worlds.

## Where it's still behind

Open Historia is a held experiment, not a finished platform. The map detail and campaign pacing are prototype-grade, and there is no multiplayer or community scenario marketplace yet. If you want the mature product, Pax Historia is it — if you want the open, hackable, no-credits version to play with or build on, try this one.

## Your keys, your provider

Pick Anthropic Claude, OpenAI, Google Gemini, DeepSeek, a local OpenAI-compatible model, or the shared free gateway on setup. Provider keys stay in your session and go only to the provider you chose.

## Start an alternate history

Pick a scenario, choose a nation, give your first order.

[Play Open Historia](https://historia.aliveville.com/play)
